errors.english: Should not be despised in this world,
errors.why: The verse says the person seeking happiness should do what is uncensured in this world and brings happiness in the next; 'not censured' qualifies the action, not the person.

fix.find:
Should not be despised in this world,
And should perform whatever leads
fix.replace:
Should do what is not censured in this world
And whatever leads

errors.english: act like a spiritual teacher or a lord toward others
errors.why: Having abandoned pride one should not disdain others (continuing on the next side), treating them as gurus or masters; it is not an instruction to act as a teacher or lord toward others.

note: A good rendering of the buffalo-sacrifice and butcher's-son exempla; the verse on uncensured conduct and the closing clause on pride are misconstrued.

errors.english: causes the mind that perceives the absence of an entity to cut the continuity
errors.why: The cognition of absence (instrumental) cuts the continuum of the entity-cognition by producing an incompatible vāsanā-cause; the English makes the entity-cognition the producer and the absence-cognition merely caused to cut.

errors.english: If one were to take this to an extreme, even the conception of blue would not be able to act as an incompatible latent tendency for it
errors.why: The Tibetan answers the over-extension worry: the conception of blue (which would cause over-extension) cannot make that vāsanā incompatible, so it does not cut suffering; the English turns this into a conditional absurdity.

note: Generally follows a difficult Pramāṇa argument on co-presence of conceptions, with some blurring of who cuts whose continuum.

errors.english: Well then, how is fire perceived as fire? By perceiving the common characteristic of sharpness
errors.why: ཇི་ལྟར ... དེ་བཞིན་དུ is a 'just as ... so' correlative opening the opponent's analogy (just as fire is superimposed on the brahmin boy, so the earlier colours are superimposed), not a question about how fire is perceived.

fix.find: Well then, how is fire perceived as fire? By perceiving
fix.replace: Suppose it is said: just as, when fire has been apprehended as fire, by perceiving

errors.english: If this were to change, these two would not be the same.
errors.why: 'These two are not alike' is the author's reply rejecting the analogy of the blooming forest; the English folds it into a conditional.

errors.english: This is because everything is known through the functioning of the eye.
errors.why: This states the unwanted consequence (everything would be known by the eye's operation), not a thesis the author asserts.

note: The sequence of objection and reply on variegated cognition is partly misparsed, though the root verses are correctly identified.

errors.english: It describes the kinds of Buddha-fields present in those Bodhisattvas
errors.why: The Tibetan speaks of what kind of bodhisattvas there were in the Buddha-fields of those Buddhas; the containment is reversed.

fix.find: It describes the kinds of Buddha-fields present in those Bodhisattvas,
fix.replace: It describes what kinds of Bodhisattvas there were in the Buddha-fields of those Buddhas,

errors.english: single, spontaneously appearing (nisyanda-kaya)
errors.why: རྒྱུ་མཐུན་པའི་སྐུ is the body causally concordant (niṣyanda); 'spontaneously appearing' is not its meaning (effortlessness is expressed separately by འབད་པ་མེད་པ).

note: A sound rendering of the list of past deeds shown in one body, with one inverted clause about bodhisattvas and Buddha-fields.

errors.english: the third sign [note: the third characteristic of a logical reason: the absence of the reason in the heterologue or "non-concordant class"]
errors.why: With ཚུལ་ ending the previous side this is ཚུལ་གསུམ་པའི་རྟགས, the reason possessing the three characteristics (trairūpya), not 'the third sign'.

fix.find: the third sign [note: the third characteristic of a logical reason: the absence of the reason in the heterologue or "non-concordant class"]
fix.replace: the reason possessing the three characteristics (trairūpya)

errors.english: where the reason exists in all instances of the property to be proven
errors.why: Anvaya is that the presence of the reason is pervaded everywhere by the presence of the probandum (wherever the reason, there the property); the English reverses the direction of pervasion.

fix.find: where the reason exists in all instances of the property to be proven
fix.replace: where, in all cases, the presence of the reason is pervaded by the presence of the property to be proven

errors.english: the presence of the reason wherever the property is present
errors.why: The inline gloss on anvaya inverts it: positive concomitance is the presence of the property wherever the reason is present.

fix.find: the presence of the reason wherever the property is present
fix.replace: the presence of the property wherever the reason is present

errors.english: because you authors of treatises distinguish
errors.why: It is the treatise author (Dharmakīrti) who specifies the restriction to sapakṣa/vipakṣa, as the opponent addressed here holds; 'you authors of treatises' conflates the two.

note: The argument about why 'certainty' (niścita) is mentioned is followed, but the trairūpya term and the direction of anvaya are rendered wrongly.

errors.english: An connection with the actual nature of the subject
errors.why: In this list of viruddha types (cf. ཆོས་ཀྱི་རང་གི་ངོ་བོ་དང་འགལ་བ on the previous side) the reading should be འགལ་བ, contradiction with the nature of the subject, as the example shows.

errors.english: By seeing that non-existent things like a rabbit's horns do not exist, this argument
errors.why: The reason 'uncreated' is seen in non-existents such as the rabbit's horn, and so proves space non-existent; it is not about seeing that rabbit's horns do not exist.

note: The discussion of the word 'itself' (svayam) in the thesis definition is rendered clearly; the hetu-example is misconstrued.

errors.english: There is no offense for one carried by miraculous power
errors.why: The case is carrying (goods) across by magical power, as the following ཁྱེར་བ་པོ 'carrier' shows, not the monk being carried.

errors.english: for one who possesses a mind lacking the intent to deceive
errors.why: ཡིད་མི་ཆེས་པ means disbelief or lack of confidence, not absence of an intent to deceive.

errors.english: but has no specific purpose [note: to evade], there is no downfall
errors.why: The contrast is between magic that does not need a carrier standing on ground within the boundary (no offence) and one that does (sthūlātyaya); the bracketed 'intent' notes are invented.

note: The toll-evasion rulings are mostly intelligible, but the treatment of magical carrying at the end is misread.
A faithful rendering of the argument for the Mahāyāna as buddhavacana, including the patriarchal lineage and the parity argument.

errors.english: (Upali) the Buddha's disciple foremost in knowledge of monastic law replied, "They should be given."
errors.why: Upāli is the questioner; ཉེ་བ་འཁོར is the vocative in the Buddha's answer: 'Upāli, it should be given.'

fix.find: (Upali) the Buddha's disciple foremost in knowledge of monastic law replied, "They should be given."
fix.replace: The Buddha replied, "Upāli, they should be given."

errors.english: the son will not return as the master of the father's house
errors.why: The reason is that the expelled son does not lose his status as an owner of the father's household, which is why goods may be accepted from him.

fix.find: the son will not return as the master of the father's house
fix.replace: the son is not excluded from being an owner of the father's household

errors.english: if they do not wear them
errors.why: Here བགོ means to divide or share out (jointly held goods not yet divided), not to wear.

note: The Vinaya rulings on entrusted goods are partly followed, but the speaker of the canonical answer and the reason for accepting from an expelled son are wrong.

errors.english: regarding the meaning of reality which possesses equanimity

errors.english: they engage in outward conduct
errors.why: PV bāhyacintā: they engage in consideration (analysis) of external objects, not 'outward conduct'.

errors.english: That [note: the ultimate nature] is not of the same category as those [note: ordinary perceptions].
errors.why: The verse says that those who do not see the supreme are not fit for (knowers of) reality, as the commentary later repeats; the notes impose a different reading.

note: The commentary on PV III's elephant-closing verse is misconstrued at its key points, though the surrounding argument on duality is rendered adequately.
